key_insight: Imaging-based measures of residual meningioma after surgery—especially volumetric quantification—predicted recurrence better than traditional Simpson grading.
clinical_relevance: A structured MRI-report approach can scale postoperative assessment beyond subjective surgical grading and may better support follow-up risk stratification.
method: Retrospective multicentre cohort of 912 primary cranial meningioma resections (2006–2025).
Postoperative MRI reports were classified with TF-IDF + linear SVM into radiological gross-total vs subtotal resection.
Residual tumour volume was segmented on contrast-enhanced MRI and tested alongside Simpson grade in Cox recurrence models.
evidence_signal: In adjusted analysis, recurrence hazard rose with Simpson grade, radiological grade, and log residual volume; optimism-corrected concordance improved from 0.692 to 0.733 to 0.748, respectively.
watch_item: Report-derived grading depends on imaging quality, report wording, and timing of postoperative MRI, so performance may vary across sites and workflows.
paper_title: Redefining Extent Of Resection After Meningioma Surgery: a Multicentre Observational Machine Learning Analysis Comparing Simpson, Radiological and Volumetric Grading
